notes: Numeric lookup deep inside NFM A6.2's freshwater oxygen-solubility table (table 6.2-2). Claims: do-t622-20c-750-897-01 (8.97 mg/L at 750 mmHg, 9.09 at 760, 20.0 C), do-t622-35c-760-695-01 (6.95 mg/L at 760 mmHg, 35.0 C). Both claims sit on caption- and column-header-bearing chunks (indices 59 and 62), not on the headerless continuation grids listed in the a6.2 summary notes, so the row/column pairing is honestly retrievable. Nothing in the direct-feed slice tabulates solubility against temperature and pressure — the operator source-of-truth only gives healthy-range bands (6-11 mg/L freshwater), which is the wrong kind of answer. Expected to favor rag: the value exists in exactly one place in the corpus, ~65 percent of the way through a 91-chunk document, and no amount of the slice or general knowledge produces 9.09 and 6.95 from the same table.

turns.content: Water at one of our sites was 20 °C this morning and the barometer on the pod read 760 mm. If that water were fully saturated with air, what should the DO sensor be showing?

must_contain: Attributes the value to the freshwater table in the USGS NFM chapter on dissolved oxygen (table 6.2-2)
States the figure is for fresh water, before any salinity correction
must_not: Invents a value for 20 °C at 760 mmHg that is not the table's
Answers with the operator baseline band (6-11 mg/L healthy freshwater) instead of the manual's table value
Cites the Atlas Scientific Industrial DO probe datasheet, which contains no solubility table

turns.content: By late afternoon the same spot was up to 35 °C and the barometer hadn't moved. How much does that change the number?

must_contain: States the ceiling falls by roughly 2 mg/L compared with the 20 °C value
Takes both figures from the same USGS table rather than mixing sources
must_not: Interpolates or estimates instead of reading the 35.0 °C row
States or implies that warmer water can hold more oxygen
Invents a barometric correction the question did not ask for
